scalars.scalar_value: Two (2) years of experience in hospice.

items.item_text: Valid California Registered Nurse License without restriction
American Heart Association (AHA) or American Red Cross Basic Life Support (BLS) or UC Davis Health CPR
Required to hold a valid California driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program
Two (2) years of experience in hospice.
Hospice experience in clinical coordination, charge nurse, and Quality Assessment Performance Improvement (QAPI).

The Home Care Services (HCS) Clinical Patient Navigator 4 (Hospice RN Navigator) is a technical, autonomous leader in hospice care, and has the ability to develop and lead teams/programs, direct patient care, and guide/improve clinical practice. The primary goals for the Hospice RN Navigator are to increase patient and staff satisfaction, optimize care, and improve outcomes.
50% - Clinical Care Coordination, Navigation, and Education
5% - Professional Development
Verification of graduation from an accredited school of nursing
Adapts to change in a positive, professional and productive manner.
Commitment to continual excellence and performance improvement in patient-centered care.

Advanced clinical knowledge in a variety of modalities, or signiﬁcant expertise in a specialty area. Advanced ability to assess patient needs and make appropriate referrals for specialized support services and programs.

Advanced skills in assessing patient’s grievances and locating appropriate resources to get issues resolved. Advanced skills to intervene and assist with patient’s questions or concerns about treatment plan.
Advanced patient care skills, working with a high volume and high expectations customer base. Strong ability to support patients with a wide variety of clinical and non-clinical needs.

Advanced skills and expertise working in a complex, multi-divisional environment, with proven ability to initiate projects and lead teams, prioritize tasks, and direct projects successfully from inception to completion on task and on schedule.
Skills to perform in-depth chart analysis to provide accurate information in a concise, informative manner.
Demonstrated knowledge with Windows-based software including Microsoft word, Excel, Outlook. Strong Knowledge of clinical based computer systems and software. Advanced computer skills.
Knowledge of care/services provided in differing levels of care, i.e., ambulatory, and institutional settings, community-based resources, SNF, Home Health, Hospice, and Palliative Care.
Analytical skills to identify and obtain pertinent data from multiple sources and work with culturally diverse patients and families with multiple needs or disabilities.
Ability to make independent judgments based on clinical knowledge.
Ability to work with all levels of staff, both inter- and intra-departmental to create a cooperative relationship and positive work environment. Utilizes tact and diplomacy skills at all times.
Effective time management skills to accommodate special projects, deadlines, and priorities.
Ability to read, write, speak, and understand the English language.
Knowledge of current trends in nursing and interdisciplinary clinical practice.
Demonstrates excellent clinical judgment skills, accountability, and professionalism in patient-centered care.
Demonstrates accountability and professionalism.
Knowledge of legal implications in clinical practice and documentation.
Knowledge of performance improvement and evidence-based practice.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills to effectively communicate with a diverse patient and staff population in a clear, concise, and professional manner.
Ability to utilize medical terminology appropriately.
Ability to work successfully in stressful situations and remain calm under pressure.
Knowledge of legal and ethical considerations in healthcare and clinical practice including confidentiality, patient rights, and documentation standards relevant to position.

Ability to assess, plan, implement, and evaluate patient care, taking into consideration protective interventions, development (behavioral and physical), and physiological characteristics specific to the patients.
Effective organizational and developmental skills that improve productivity and demonstrate a commitment to ongoing learning.
Ability to provide and accept guidance and criticism.
